items.title: Stanley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998
items.q: I didn’t hear Red Norvo’s band.

ctx.x: Yes it was the lowest class. We didn’t want to waste any money on that. But it was rather regrettable because it was very rough, and if you’re in the front of the nose, it comes down and as it hits the waves — I was in bed for two or three days there. And we were a day late getting into New York. But it played out very well because it was just the height of — almost the height of the Swing Era, ‘37. I heard, in three weeks I heard eighteen big bands of quality. And I was rather disgusted I remember because I…

items.title: 56799_Red Norvo oral history interview
items.q: Stanley and I were married right the next year

ctx.x: show, I think at that time, just started. He was in doing that show and they were living at the Essex House, I remember. So they came over, Joe from the shows and Sally and a bunch of them, so we were in the kitchen he's telling me how fond he was of Mildred and everything. He said, 'You know, when I came down to Los Angeles,' he said, 'Mildred was working in a nightclub,' and he said, 'That first night we came in the club and,' he said, 'went home and she pulled up her dress and she had these bloomers on, and…

Oh, how funny. Oh, gosh. Well listen you know because when I left I left in -- well I went into the Army in '42, you know, and then I came back in '45 and Stanley and I were married right the next year, so -- yeah. It's work- ing -- well we were talking about Mildred, Red, and we sort of jumped ahead a little bit, but it just seemed to me that it's important to talk about Mildred because there aren't the -- there aren't people to talk about Mildred the same way anymore and as you say the myths don't get built up…
